sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 新老听众们，无论你们身处世界的哪个角落，非常高兴大家能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们要一起剖析20多岁时的心理学。

sentences.en: Today, let's talk about destiny or something that feels strangely attached to it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来聊聊命运，或者某种感觉与其有着奇妙联系的事物。

sentences.en: Let's talk about personality, whether it's fixed or it can be changed, how it shapes our future, our beliefs, maybe even how happy we are.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈性格，看看它是固定不变的还是可以改变的，它是如何塑造我们的未来、我们的信念，甚至可能决定我们的幸福感。

sentences.en: Personality is like a little bit of a black box.
sentences.zh: 性格就像是一个小小的黑箱。

sentences.en: Like we know it's shaped by nature and nurture.
sentences.zh: 比如我们知道它是由先天和后天共同塑造的。

sentences.en: We know that genetics are involved, how we were raised is kind of involved.
sentences.zh: 我们知道遗传因素在其中，我们的成长环境也多多少少有影响。

sentences.en: But I think as we get older, we become more aware of the parts of ourselves that are holding us back and that we really would wish for something different.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得随着年龄增长，我们会越来越清楚地意识到自己身上那些阻碍我们前进、让我们真心希望有所改变的部分。

sentences.en: Well, today I have the honor of interviewing someone who has investigated that very possibility.
sentences.zh: 好吧，今天我有幸采访了一位深入研究过这种可能性的人。

sentences.en: What if we could be ourselves but better by rewiring our personality?
sentences.zh: 如果我们能通过重塑性格来保持自我但变得更好，会怎样呢？

sentences.en: I want to welcome on author and journalist,
sentences.zh: 让我们欢迎作家兼记者，

sentences.en: Olga Hazan.
sentences.zh: 奥尔加·哈赞（Olga Hazan）。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你来到我们节目。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 不用客气。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: I'm very, very excited for this episode and this topic in general.
sentences.zh: 我非常非常期待这期节目以及这个总体话题。

sentences.en: But before we kind of jump into it, can you briefly introduce yourself to the audience and your work?
sentences.zh: 但在我们深入探讨之前，你能否向听众简要介绍一下你自己和你的工作？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: My name is Olga Hazan and I'm a staff writer at The Atlantic Magazine and I'm also an author of books.
sentences.zh: 我叫奥尔加·哈赞，我是《大西洋月刊》（The Atlantic）的专职记者，我也是一名图书作者。

sentences.en: This is my second book and it is actually kind of stems from a cover story I did for The Atlantic a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 这是我的第二本书，它其实源于几年前我为《大西洋月刊》写的一篇封面报道。

sentences.en: So that's my backstory.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的背景故事。

sentences.en: And you're not going to give us any spoilers.
sentences.zh: 而且你不会给我们任何剧透。

sentences.en: I feel like the cover story, like you go into it kind of in the book, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得那篇封面报道的内容，你在书里也有深入探讨，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I can give you a spoiler.
sentences.zh: 对，我可以给你剧透一下。

sentences.en: So the cover story, I kind of experimented very lightly with changing my personality, but then I kind of realized that I needed to do more and that it, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以那篇封面报道里，我非常轻量地尝试了改变我的性格，但后来我发现我需要做更多，而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: kind of letting up on the experiment, I backtracked.
sentences.zh: 随着我对实验的放松，我又退缩了。

sentences.en: I noticed that I was sort of falling back into old patterns.
sentences.zh: 我注意到自己似乎又落入了旧有的模式中。

sentences.en: So the book is really an overview of the five traits of personality,
sentences.zh: 所以这本书实际上是对性格五个特质的概述，

sentences.en: my personal attempts to change on three of them.
sentences.zh: 以及我个人对其中三个特质做出改变的尝试。

sentences.en: And because the other two, I actually don't need to change.
sentences.zh: 因为另外两个特质，我其实不需要改变。

sentences.en: They're fine.
sentences.zh: 它们很好。

sentences.en: They're very high in me as it is.
sentences.zh: 在我身上本来就很强。

sentences.en: But I do interview other people who increased on those traits through various methods.
sentences.zh: 不过我也采访了其他人，他们通过各种方法在这些特质上得到了提升。

sentences.en: We're going to get to that because I feel like it's such an interesting premise.
sentences.zh: 我们马上会聊到这个，因为我觉得这是一个非常有趣的前提。

sentences.en: But I do also want to talk about how you became a journalist, how you became a writer.
sentences.zh: 但我也想聊聊你是怎么成为一名记者、一名作家的。

sentences.en: I think as much as I love interviewing people about the very, you know, amazing niche things that they're doing and they're like, whether it's psychology or neuroscience
sentences.zh: 我想，尽管我很喜欢采访人们做的那些非常了不起、很小众的事情，比如心理学、神经科学

sentences.en: or anything like that, you know, this podcast is for people in their 20s and a lot of people probably aspire to do what you do.
sentences.zh: 或者诸如此类的领域，但这个播客是为20多岁的年轻人准备的，很多人可能都渴望做你现在做的事。

sentences.en: Can you kind of talk us through how you got from maybe graduating high school to where you are now?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我们聊聊你是怎么从高中毕业走到今天的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 那是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Just give us an overview of your entire life.
sentences.zh: 那就大致讲讲你的一生吧。

sentences.en: Please and thank you.
sentences.zh: 拜托啦，谢谢。

sentences.en: Graduated from high school like 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 大概20年前高中毕业。

sentences.en: Then I went to college, did not major in journalism, but really found myself drawn to journalism.
sentences.zh: 然后我上了大学，主修的不是新闻学，但发现自己真的很被新闻学吸引。

sentences.en: I did an internship in journalism.
sentences.zh: 我做过一份新闻实习。

sentences.en: And then I went to graduate school after I graduated from college, which is not like a necessary step for anyone listening at home, but it is something that I did.
sentences.zh: 大学毕业后我又去读了研究生，这对于在听节目的任何人来说都不是必须的一步，但这是我走过的一条路。

sentences.en: Then I got a job at the Washington Post out of graduate school and I worked there for a brief time.
sentences.zh: 研究生毕业后，我在《华盛顿邮报》（The Washington Post）找到了一份工作，并在那里工作了一小段时间。

sentences.en: And then I moved to the Atlantic in 2013.
sentences.zh: 接着我在2013年加入了《大西洋月刊》。

sentences.en: And I've worked at the Atlantic ever since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后我一直呆在《大西洋月刊》。

sentences.en: And I've done a couple of different jobs there, but I've mostly been a writer
sentences.zh: 我在那里做过几个不同的岗位，但主要还是担任记者，

sentences.en: covering like health and human behavior.
sentences.zh: 报道健康和人类行为方面的内容。

sentences.en: Well, that's my, that's the perfect topic for this.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了，这绝对是这期节目的绝佳主题。

sentences.en: Do you remember like what your first big piece of writing was?
sentences.zh: 你还记得你的第一篇重要作品是什么吗？

sentences.en: Like your first article where you were like, oh my gosh, like I'm a journaliSt.
sentences.zh: 就像你的第一篇文章，当时让你觉得，哦天哪，我真的是个记者了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That probably was.
sentences.zh: 那可能就是……

sentences.en: So when I did my internship in college, I wrote one story during that internship.
sentences.zh: 我在上大学时实习期间，写过一篇报道。

sentences.en: It was complex why I only wrote one, but that was like the amount that I was allowed to write.
sentences.zh: 为什么只写了一篇说来话长，但那就是当时允许我写的字数额度。

sentences.en: Um, and it was about online gaming addiction.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是关于网络游戏成瘾的。

sentences.en: Um, and, uh, I remember when it came out, I felt so just accomplished.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，我记得文章发表的时候，我感到无比的成就感。

sentences.en: Like I was like, yes, like my life is all coming together.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，太棒了，我的人生一切都在步入正轨。

sentences.en: And of course, like,
sentences.zh: 当然啦，

sentences.en: I wouldn't be a full-time writer for I think eight years after that.
sentences.zh: 在那之后大概八年时间里，我都还没能成为一名全职作家。

sentences.en: Um, uh, but it was, it was like very, uh, good motivation to keep going.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过，那确实是非常好的动力，促使我坚持下去。

sentences.en: You know, I love stories like that where it's like, okay, just because your dream isn't happening right now doesn't mean that it's not going to come true eventually.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我很喜欢这样的故事：即使你的梦想现在没有实现，也不意味着它最终不会成真。

sentences.en: Like, as you said, you had this, like, what sounds like this big accomplished moment and, you know, it really didn't come full circle until, what did you say?
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，你当时有了这种听起来非常了不起的成就感，而且，你知道的，直到——你刚才怎么说来着？

sentences.en: Like 10 years ago, almost maybe 12 years ago, which we love hearing those stories on the show.
sentences.zh: 大约10年前，差不多快12年前，事情才真正圆满，我们很喜欢在节目里听到这样的故事。

sentences.en: Um, let's talk about this book.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们来聊聊这本书。

sentences.en: The premise of this book was basically that cover story and this idea that you wanted to change your personality.
sentences.zh: 这本书的前提基本上就是那篇封面报道以及你想改变性格的想法。

sentences.en: Why did you feel like it was necessary?
sentences.zh: 你为什么觉得这很有必要？

sentences.en: Like, why did you feel like you had to do that?
sentences.zh: 比如，为什么你觉得你非得这么做不可？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So your personality, you know, a lot of people think it's sort of like what you like or dislike or sort of the kinds of things you say or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以关于性格，你知道的，很多人觉得它就像是你喜欢或讨厌什么，或者你说话的方式之类的。

sentences.en: Um, but it's really a lot about your reactions to situations and kind of like something comes across your way and are you like, yes, let's do it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但它其实很大程度上关乎你对各种情况的反应，就好像有什么事落到你头上时，你是会说“太好了，我们干吧”，

sentences.en: Or are you like, oh, I don't know about that.
sentences.zh: 还是会说“呃，我不太确定这个”。

sentences.en: Or, you know, it's kind of like how, how you interact with the world.
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道的，这其实关乎你如何与这个世界互动。

sentences.en: Um, and I noticed that a lot of how I was interacting with the world, uh,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我注意到我与世界互动的方式中，有很多部分，

sentences.en: was not helping me really.
sentences.zh: 其实并没有真正帮到我。

sentences.en: Um, so the intro to the book kind of gives a good overview of this, but I had this day,
sentences.zh: 所以书的引言部分对此做了一个很好的概述，但我当时经历了这样一天，

sentences.en: this is before I had a kid and it was like, now having had a kid,
sentences.zh: 那是生孩子之前的事了，现在有了孩子之后，

sentences.en: I'm like, wow, this was actually like a fantastic day.
sentences.zh: 我心想，哇，这其实是个绝佳的一天啊。

sentences.en: I should have just appreciated it.
sentences.zh: 我当时真应该好好珍惜它的。

sentences.en: But, you know, it was like, I got stuck in traffic.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，情况是这样的：我遭遇了交通堵塞。

sentences.en: I got a bad haircut.
sentences.zh: 剪了个很糟糕的发型。

sentences.en: I got photos taken that looked really bad.
sentences.zh: 拍出来的照片看起来丑极了。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: I had a stressful thing where I had to like pick my mom up at the airport, but I had to go grocery shopping before, but the, like, there was like a delay at the grocery store
sentences.zh: 我还碰上一件压力很大的事，我得去机场接我妈妈，但在那之前我还得去买菜，结果呢，超市那边排队耽搁了，

sentences.en: and then I was going to be late to pick up my mom and it was like this whole thing and I just had a meltdown.
sentences.zh: 然后我去接我妈妈就要迟到了，整个过程就是一团糟，我当时彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: I got back to my Airbnb that I was staying in and I like drank wine and like cried to my boyfriend at the time and was just like, I hate everything.
sentences.zh: 回到我当时住的民宿后，我喝着酒，向当时的男友痛哭流涕，直呼我讨厌这一切。

sentences.en: Um, and then I kind of got to thinking and I was like, even like me saying that now to you,
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后我开始反思，甚至现在我把这事说给你听，

sentences.en: I'm like, wow, that is so whiny and like unappreciative of the fact that like that day, you know, I was able to buy groceries.
sentences.zh: 我都觉得，哇，这也太爱抱怨了吧，简直太不懂得感恩了，明明那天，你知道的，我有能力去买菜，

sentences.en: I was in Miami.
sentences.zh: 我在迈阿密。

sentences.en: Like, I got myself to Miami.
sentences.zh: 你看，我自己去了迈阿密。

sentences.en: Uh,
sentences.zh: 呃，

sentences.en: I, you know, was getting a haircut, like spa day for me.
sentences.zh: 我当时在弄头发，对我来说就像是做水疗的一天。
